questions.q: Express $\dfrac{5x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: Write $\dfrac{5x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)}=\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{x+2}$. Multiply through: $5x+7=A(x+2)+B(x+1)$. At $x=-1$: $2=A(1)$, so $A=2$. At $x=-2$: $-3=B(-1)$, so $B=3$. Result: $\dfrac{2}{x+1}+\dfrac{3}{x+2}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{3x-1}{x(x-3)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: Write $\dfrac{3x-1}{x(x-3)}=\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{B}{x-3}$. Then $3x-1=A(x-3)+Bx$. At $x=0$: $-1=-3A$, so $A=\dfrac{1}{3}$. At $x=3$: $8=3B$, so $B=\dfrac{8}{3}$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{3x}+\dfrac{8}{3(x-3)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{4x+1}{(x-1)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{(x-1)^2}$.
questions.answer: $4x+1=A(x-1)+B$. At $x=1$: $5=B$. Comparing coefficients of $x$: $A=4$. Result: $\dfrac{4}{x-1}+\dfrac{5}{(x-1)^2}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2x^2-3x+1}{x(x-1)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{B}{x-1}+\dfrac{C}{(x-1)^2}$.
questions.answer: $2x^2-3x+1=A(x-1)^2+Bx(x-1)+Cx$. At $x=0$: $1=A(1)$, so $A=1$. At $x=1$: $0=C(1)$, so $C=0$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $2=A+B$, so $B=2-1=1$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{x}+\dfrac{1}{x-1}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{3x^2+2}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$.
questions.answer: $3x^2+2=A(x^2+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1)$. At $x=1$: $5=2A$, so $A=\dfrac{5}{2}$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $3=A+B$, so $B=3-\dfrac{5}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}$. Comparing constants: $2=A-C$, so $C=A-2=\dfrac{1}{2}$. Result: $\dfrac{5}{2(x-1)}+\dfrac{x+1}{2(x^2+1)}$.

questions.q: Use partial fractions to evaluate $\int\dfrac{5x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)}\,dx$, using the decomposition found earlier in this worksheet.
questions.answer: From earlier: $\dfrac{5x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)}=\dfrac{2}{x+1}+\dfrac{3}{x+2}$. So $\int\dfrac{5x+7}{(x+1)(x+2)}\,dx=2\ln|x+1|+3\ln|x+2|+C$.

sections.heading: Applying partial fractions to a binomial series expansion

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{1}{(1-x)(1-2x)}$ in partial fractions, then use the result to write the first three terms of its series expansion in ascending powers of $x$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{1}{(1-x)(1-2x)}=\dfrac{A}{1-x}+\dfrac{B}{1-2x}$. Then $1=A(1-2x)+B(1-x)$. At $x=1$: $1=A(-1)$, so $A=-1$. At $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $1=B\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, so $B=2$. Result: $\dfrac{-1}{1-x}+\dfrac{2}{1-2x}$. Expanding each geometric series: $-1(1+x+x^2+\cdots)+2(1+2x+4x^2+\cdots)=(-1+2)+(-1+4)x+(-1+8)x^2+\cdots=1+3x+7x^2+\cdots$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{7-x}{(x+1)(x-2)}$ in partial fractions.
Express $\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x(x+1)}$ in partial fractions. (Hint: the degree of the numerator equals the degree of the denominator, so first perform polynomial division.)
questions.answer: Since numerator and denominator are both degree 2, divide first: $\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x^2+x}=1+\dfrac{1}{x^2+x}=1+\dfrac{1}{x(x+1)}$. Decompose $\dfrac{1}{x(x+1)}=\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{B}{x+1}$: $1=A(x+1)+Bx$. At $x=0$: $A=1$. At $x=-1$: $B=-1$. Result: $1+\dfrac{1}{x}-\dfrac{1}{x+1}$.

sections.heading: Applying partial fractions to a rate problem

questions.q: A population model gives the rate of change $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{P(10-P)}$. Express $\dfrac{1}{P(10-P)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{P}+\dfrac{B}{10-P}$.
questions.answer: $1=A(10-P)+BP$. At $P=0$: $1=10A$, so $A=\dfrac{1}{10}$. At $P=10$: $1=10B$, so $B=\dfrac{1}{10}$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{10P}+\dfrac{1}{10(10-P)}$ — a decomposition commonly used to solve logistic-growth differential equations by separation of variables.

sections.heading: Partial fractions with three distinct linear factors

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{6x^2-2x-1}{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)}$ in partial fractions.

sections.heading: Partial fractions with an improper fraction and repeated factor

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x^3}{(x-1)^2}$ in partial fractions, first performing polynomial division since the numerator has higher degree than the denominator.
questions.answer: Divide $x^3$ by $(x-1)^2=x^2-2x+1$: $x^3\div(x^2-2x+1)=x+2$ remainder $3x-2$. So $\dfrac{x^3}{(x-1)^2}=x+2+\dfrac{3x-2}{(x-1)^2}$. Decompose the remainder: $\dfrac{3x-2}{(x-1)^2}=\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{(x-1)^2}$, giving $3x-2=A(x-1)+B$. At $x=1$: $1=B$. Comparing $x$ coefficients: $A=3$. Result: $x+2+\dfrac{3}{x-1}+\dfrac{1}{(x-1)^2}$.

sections.heading: Using partial fractions to sum a series

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)}$ in partial fractions, and use the result to find $\sum_{n=1}^{4}\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)}$ by telescoping.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)}=\dfrac{1}{n}-\dfrac{1}{n+1}$ (standard decomposition with $A=1$, $B=-1$). Summing from $n=1$ to $4$: $\left(1-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)=1-\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{4}{5}$, since all the middle terms cancel (telescope).

sections.heading: Decomposing a fraction with a repeated quadratic-adjacent structure

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x+5}{(x-1)(x+1)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{x+1}+\dfrac{C}{(x+1)^2}$.
Express $\dfrac{2x^2+x-1}{x^2(x+1)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{B}{x^2}+\dfrac{C}{x+1}$.
questions.answer: $2x^2+x-1=Ax(x+1)+B(x+1)+Cx^2$. At $x=0$: $-1=B(1)$, so $B=-1$. At $x=-1$: $0=C(1)$, so $C=0$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $2=A+C=A$, so $A=2$. Result: $\dfrac{2}{x}-\dfrac{1}{x^2}$.

questions.q: Use partial fractions to find the Maclaurin (power series) expansion of $\dfrac{1}{(1-x)(2-x)}$ up to the term in $x^2$, first decomposing into the form $\dfrac{A}{1-x}+\dfrac{B}{2-x}$.
questions.answer: $1=A(2-x)+B(1-x)$. At $x=1$: $1=A(1)$, so $A=1$. At $x=2$: $1=B(-1)$, so $B=-1$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{1-x}-\dfrac{1}{2-x}=\dfrac{1}{1-x}-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{1-x/2}$. Expanding each as a geometric series: $(1+x+x^2+\cdots)-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1+\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\cdots\right)=\left(1-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)x+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{8}\right)x^2+\cdots=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{3}{4}x+\dfrac{7}{8}x^2+\cdots$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{4x^2-5x-15}{(x+1)(x-2)(x+3)}$ in partial fractions, using the cover-up method (evaluating the numerator at each root while covering the matching factor in the denominator).

A chemical reaction's rate is modeled by $\dfrac{dC}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{(C+2)(C-1)}$, where $C$ is a concentration. Express $\dfrac{1}{(C+2)(C-1)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{C+2}+\dfrac{B}{C-1}$, and then use the result to write the general antiderivative $\int\dfrac{1}{(C+2)(C-1)}\,dC$ in terms of natural logarithms.
questions.answer: $1=A(C-1)+B(C+2)$. At $C=1$: $1=B(3)$, so $B=\dfrac{1}{3}$. At $C=-2$: $1=A(-3)$, so $A=-\dfrac{1}{3}$. Result: $\dfrac{-1/3}{C+2}+\dfrac{1/3}{C-1}$. Integrating: $\int\dfrac{1}{(C+2)(C-1)}\,dC=-\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|C+2|+\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|C-1|+K=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln\left|\dfrac{C-1}{C+2}\right|+K$.

questions.q: Use the decomposition $\dfrac{1}{3x}+\dfrac{8}{3(x-3)}$ found earlier in this worksheet for $\dfrac{3x-1}{x(x-3)}$ to evaluate $\int_4^5\dfrac{3x-1}{x(x-3)}\,dx$, giving your answer as a single logarithm expression.
questions.answer: $\int\dfrac{3x-1}{x(x-3)}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|x|+\dfrac{8}{3}\ln|x-3|+C$. Evaluating from $4$ to $5$: $\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\ln5+\dfrac{8}{3}\ln2\right]-\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\ln4+\dfrac{8}{3}\ln1\right]=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln5+\dfrac{8}{3}\ln2-\dfrac{1}{3}\ln4=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln\dfrac{5}{4}+\dfrac{8}{3}\ln2$.

questions.q: This question has three parts. (a) Factor $x^2-4$ and hence express $\dfrac{x+8}{x^2-4}$ in partial fractions. (b) Use your result from part (a) to write down $\int\dfrac{x+8}{x^2-4}\,dx$. (c) Hence evaluate $\int_3^5\dfrac{x+8}{x^2-4}\,dx$, giving your answer as a single expression involving natural logarithms.
questions.answer: (a) Factor $x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)$, so $\dfrac{x+8}{(x-2)(x+2)}=\dfrac{A}{x-2}+\dfrac{B}{x+2}$. Then $x+8=A(x+2)+B(x-2)$. At $x=2$: $10=4A$, so $A=\dfrac{5}{2}$. At $x=-2$: $6=-4B$, so $B=-\dfrac{3}{2}$. Result: $\dfrac{5/2}{x-2}-\dfrac{3/2}{x+2}$. (b) $\int\dfrac{x+8}{x^2-4}\,dx=\dfrac{5}{2}\ln|x-2|-\dfrac{3}{2}\ln|x+2|+C$. (c) Evaluating from $3$ to $5$: $\left[\dfrac{5}{2}\ln3-\dfrac{3}{2}\ln7\right]-\left[\dfrac{5}{2}\ln1-\dfrac{3}{2}\ln5\right]=\dfrac{5}{2}\ln3-\dfrac{3}{2}\ln7+\dfrac{3}{2}\ln5$ (since $\ln1=0$).
